standards.wording: Identify and demonstrate general safety in accordance with government regulations, health standards, and company and/or school policy.
Apply mathematical concepts to measurement techniques.
Read, comprehend, and communicate welding terms and definitions from ANSI/AWS A3.0, Standard Welding Terms and Definitions.
Identify basic weld symbols and joints.
Use appropriate lines in welding drawing.
Read and sketch drawings.
Identify and explain the safety, parts, and operation of thermal cutting equipment.
Prepare layouts for cutting individual parts.
Perform cuts using thermal cutting processes.

competencies.name: PPE

levels.1: Needs direct prompting to select/wear PPE; may miss required items.
levels.2: Usually selects/wears correct PPE but still needs occasional reminders or corrections.
levels.3: Independently selects and correctly wears PPE appropriate to the assigned operation.
levels.4: Independently selects PPE, checks condition/fit, explains why it is required, and models correct use for others.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning ppe and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Shop Safety

levels.1: Can identify some shop rules/hazards after instruction but needs frequent reminders to follow procedures.
levels.2: Usually follows shop procedures and identifies common hazards, but needs occasional prompting.
levels.3: Consistently follows shop safety procedures and identifies common hazards.
levels.4: Anticipates hazards, explains appropriate controls, and consistently models safe behavior without prompting.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning shop safety and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Equipment Safety

levels.1: Can identify basic controls/components but needs step-by-step help to prepare, operate, or shut down equipment.
levels.2: Can perform most setup/operation/shutdown steps safely with occasional prompts.
levels.3: Safely prepares, operates, shuts down, and stores equipment.
levels.4: Performs all steps independently, verifies equipment condition, and explains safe operating/shutdown decisions.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning equipment safety and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Shop Responsibility

levels.1: Participates in cleanup/tool care when directed but needs frequent reminders.
levels.2: Usually maintains the work area and tools but may need occasional reminders about cleanup or procedures.
levels.3: Maintains an orderly work area, handles tools/materials properly, and follows cleanup procedures.
levels.4: Maintains an exemplary work area, anticipates cleanup/tool needs, and helps reinforce shop responsibility with peers.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning shop responsibility and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Measurement

levels.1: Can use measuring tools with guidance but makes frequent reading or transfer errors.
levels.2: Measures common dimensions with reasonable accuracy but still needs occasional checking or correction.
levels.3: Accurately measures material using appropriate measuring tools.
levels.4: Selects the best measuring tool, works accurately and efficiently, and independently verifies critical measurements.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning measurement and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Layout

levels.1: Can mark basic dimensions from a model/example with step-by-step guidance.
levels.2: Transfers dimensions and creates basic layouts but needs occasional help with sequence, reference edges, or accuracy.
levels.3: Transfers specified dimensions to material and creates an appropriate layout.
levels.4: Creates efficient, precise layouts independently, verifies dimensions, and considers material use/waste.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning layout and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Squareness & Accuracy

levels.1: Can check a dimension or square when directed but may not recognize an error independently.
levels.2: Checks dimensions/squareness and recognizes obvious errors with occasional prompting.
levels.3: Checks dimensions and squareness and recognizes inaccurate components.
levels.4: Systematically verifies multiple dimensions/squareness, identifies error sources, and determines an appropriate correction.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning squareness & accuracy and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Welding Terminology

levels.1: Recognizes some welding terms but uses them inconsistently or needs prompts.
levels.2: Uses common welding terms correctly in familiar situations but may need clarification on less familiar terms.
levels.3: Correctly uses common welding terminology.
levels.4: Uses terminology accurately and naturally to explain equipment, processes, problems, and solutions to others.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning welding terminology and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Weld Joints

levels.1: Can name some common joints with visual cues or teacher help.
levels.2: Identifies common joints and some applications with occasional prompting.
levels.3: Identifies common weld joints and practical applications.
levels.4: Independently selects/explains appropriate joint types for fabrication situations and justifies the choice.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning weld joints and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Weld Symbols

levels.1: Recognizes a few basic weld symbols with reference materials or prompting.
levels.2: Identifies common basic weld symbols but may need a reference for less familiar symbols.
levels.3: Identifies basic welding symbols.
levels.4: Interprets basic weld symbols independently and connects them accurately to the required joint/weld on a drawing.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning weld symbols and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Drawing Interpretation

levels.1: Can locate basic dimensions/components on a simple drawing with guidance.
levels.2: Reads simple drawings and identifies most dimensions/components but needs occasional help.
levels.3: Reads a basic welding/fabrication drawing and identifies dimensions and components.
levels.4: Independently interprets drawings, checks relationships between dimensions/components, and plans how the drawing guides fabrication.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning drawing interpretation and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Drawing Lines

levels.1: Recognizes some drawing lines but needs examples/reference materials.
levels.2: Identifies and uses common lines correctly with occasional errors or prompts.
levels.3: Identifies and appropriately uses basic lines in welding drawings.
levels.4: Uses drawing lines consistently and accurately in clear sketches/drawings and explains their purpose.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning drawing lines and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Sketching

levels.1: Creates a rough sketch with guidance but may omit important dimensions/details.
levels.2: Creates a usable basic sketch but may need help making all information clear or complete.
levels.3: Produces a basic sketch sufficient to communicate the intended part or assembly.
levels.4: Produces a clear, accurate, well-organized sketch independently with dimensions/details sufficient for another person to fabricate.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning sketching and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Cutting Equipment

levels.1: Identifies some cutting components/safety rules but needs significant prompting.
levels.2: Identifies major components and explains basic safe operation with occasional gaps.
levels.3: Identifies thermal-cutting components and explains safe operation.
levels.4: Explains component function, setup checks, hazards, and safe operation independently and can troubleshoot basic concerns.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning cutting equipment and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Cutting Setup

levels.1: Can assist with setup but needs step-by-step supervision to prepare equipment/material safely.
levels.2: Completes most setup steps safely with occasional prompts/checks.
levels.3: Safely prepares equipment and material for thermal cutting.
levels.4: Completes and verifies setup independently, identifies unsafe conditions before cutting, and corrects them appropriately.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning cutting setup and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Straight Cutting

levels.1: Can make a cut with close coaching but struggles to follow the layout consistently.
levels.2: Follows the layout with improving control; cut may wander or require cleanup.
levels.3: Performs a controlled thermal cut following an established layout.
levels.4: Maintains strong control and consistently follows layouts on more complex or demanding cuts with minimal rework.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning straight cutting and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Cutting Accuracy

levels.1: Cut is completed but dimensional accuracy/edge quality is often outside usable expectations.
levels.2: Produces generally usable cuts but accuracy or edge quality is inconsistent.
levels.3: Produces a usable cut with reasonable dimensional and edge-quality expectations.
levels.4: Produces consistently accurate, clean cuts with minimal cleanup and independently evaluates/corrects technique.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning cutting accuracy and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: SMAW Equipment & Setup

levels.1: Identifies basic SMAW equipment and can set up only with step-by-step guidance.
levels.2: Completes most SMAW setup correctly but needs occasional prompts/checks.
levels.3: Identifies equipment and safely prepares an SMAW machine.
levels.4: Sets up independently, verifies connections/settings, explains choices, and recognizes/corrects basic setup problems.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning smaw equipment & setup and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Arc Control

levels.1: Can strike an arc intermittently but struggles to maintain it without coaching.
levels.2: Strikes and maintains an arc for short periods with improving consistency.
levels.3: Strikes and maintains an arc with reasonable control.
levels.4: Starts reliably, maintains consistent arc length, and recovers from interruptions independently.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning arc control and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Stringer Beads

levels.1: Produces beads but consistency in width, travel, arc length, or angle is limited.
levels.2: Produces increasingly consistent beads with some variation or occasional coaching.
levels.3: Produces reasonably consistent stringer beads.
levels.4: Produces consistently uniform beads and independently adjusts technique based on bead appearance.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning stringer beads and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Fillet Weld

levels.1: Attempts a fillet weld but bead placement/profile is inconsistent and requires coaching.
levels.2: Produces a recognizable fillet weld with improving placement/profile but some inconsistency.
levels.3: Produces an acceptable introductory-level fillet weld.
levels.4: Produces consistently sound-looking fillet welds with good placement/profile and adjusts technique independently.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning fillet weld and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Basic Joints

levels.1: Can attempt common joints with guidance but setup/technique is inconsistent.
levels.2: Performs basic joints with partial independence; quality varies by joint.
levels.3: Performs basic welds on common joint configurations.
levels.4: Performs multiple common joints consistently and independently, adapting work/electrode angle to the joint.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning basic joints and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Welding Improvement

levels.1: Can notice that a weld has a problem after prompting but cannot yet identify a useful correction.
levels.2: Identifies obvious weld problems and suggests a correction with some guidance.
levels.3: Examines a weld, identifies an obvious problem, and makes an appropriate adjustment.
levels.4: Independently diagnoses visible problems, changes technique/settings appropriately, and verifies whether the correction improved the weld.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning welding improvement and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Fabrication Sequence

levels.1: Can follow individual fabrication steps when directed but needs help understanding the overall sequence.
levels.2: Follows most of the fabrication sequence with checkpoints/reminders.
levels.3: Follows drawing → measurement → layout → cutting → preparation → fit-up → welding.
levels.4: Plans and carries out the sequence independently, adjusts the plan when needed, and minimizes rework.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning fabrication sequence and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Fit-Up

levels.1: Can position parts with direct guidance but gaps/alignment often require correction.
levels.2: Achieves workable fit-up with occasional help checking alignment, gaps, or tack placement.
levels.3: Prepares and positions components appropriately before welding.
levels.4: Produces accurate, stable fit-up independently and anticipates how alignment/tack placement will affect the finished assembly.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning fit-up and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Project Application

levels.1: Completes portions of a project with substantial teacher direction.
levels.2: Applies several competencies to a project but still needs regular checkpoints or corrections.
levels.3: Applies multiple competencies to an instructor-selected fabrication project.
levels.4: Completes an integrated project with strong independence, accuracy, problem-solving, workmanship, and self-evaluation.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning project application and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

lessonVersions.title: Open Shop Friday - Competency Development & Reassessment
learningTargets: I am learning to use feedback and my current competency ratings to identify a skill that needs improvement.
I am learning to safely and productively practice an appropriate welding or fabrication skill.
I am learning to demonstrate improvement through new evidence when I am ready for reassessment.
successCriteria: I can identify an appropriate competency or project goal.
I can use Open Shop time safely and productively.
I can apply instructor feedback while practicing.
I can demonstrate progress or provide new evidence toward competency proficiency.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Individualized skill practice, student choice within approved activities, targeted coaching, peer collaboration where appropriate, project completion, remediation, reassessment, and extension.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, student work, weld/cut/project inspection, questioning, reassessment, and updated tracker evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select the specific WT standards connected to the competencies students are working on that Friday.

lessonVersions.title: SMAW Targeted Skill Development
learningTargets: I am learning to improve my current SMAW skill through focused practice and feedback.
I am learning to use my previous welding results to determine what I should improve next.
successCriteria: I can identify the SMAW skill I am currently developing.
I can use instructor feedback to make a specific adjustment.
I can safely use my welding time productively.
I can compare my welding attempts and identify evidence of improvement.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Differentiate practice from tracker evidence: Developing students receive foundational coaching; Proficient students progress to applications; Advanced students increase quality, independence, or troubleshooting.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, weld samples, self-assessment, questioning, updated competency evidence when meaningful improvement is demonstrated.
sourceStandardsText: WT 2.2 and/or WT 3.1 according to the actual skill; WT 1.1 when safety is an explicit instructional/assessment focus.

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Guided Work Day
learningTargets: I am learning to apply my welding and fabrication skills to make progress on my current project.
I am learning to work safely and increasingly independently through the fabrication process.
successCriteria: I can identify my current fabrication step.
I can safely select and use appropriate tools and equipment.
I can follow my drawing/design and project requirements.
I can inspect my work before progressing.
I can use class time productively and make measurable project progress.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Individual project work, coaching, problem-solving, targeted demonstrations, peer collaboration where appropriate, competency practice, and differentiated support.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, project progress, questioning, dimensional/weld/workmanship checks, competency evidence, and project-rubric criteria as appropriate.
sourceStandardsText: Select the exact WT standards students are actively applying that day.

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Completion, Remediation & Extension
learningTargets: I am learning to use feedback to determine the next step in my fabrication work.
I am learning to improve or extend my welding and fabrication skills based on my current progress.
successCriteria: I can identify the work I need to complete or improve.
I can use instructor feedback appropriately.
I can safely and productively work toward completion or improvement.
I can demonstrate progress in the targeted skill or project area.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Developing/behind: targeted completion and remediation; Proficient/on track: completion and quality improvement; Advanced/ahead: extension, precision, added joint/application, or approved independent work.
lessonVersions.assessment: Project progress, competency evidence, observation, reassessment, and applicable project-rubric criteria.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards according to the individual fabrication tasks students are completing.

lessonVersions.title: Introduction to Welding Shop Safety & PPE
learningTargets: I am learning to identify major hazards found in the welding shop.
I am learning to identify the PPE required for welding and fabrication activities.
I am learning to explain why following shop safety procedures is necessary.
successCriteria: I can identify common hazards during the shop walkthrough.
I can select the correct PPE for common welding-shop activities.
I can explain the purpose of required PPE.
I can follow established safety expectations during the class period.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Safety video segments with discussion; instructor-led shop walkthrough; hazard identification; PPE identification using actual shop equipment.
lessonVersions.assessment: Instructor questioning and observation during the safety discussion and shop walkthrough; hazard and PPE identification.

lessonVersions.title: Proper PPE & Welding Shop Safety Procedures
learningTargets: I am learning to correctly select and wear PPE for welding-shop activities.
I am learning to demonstrate safe behavior in the welding shop.
I am learning to identify unsafe conditions before beginning work.
successCriteria: I can correctly select required PPE.
I can properly wear and adjust my PPE.
I can identify unsafe conditions or behaviors.
I can demonstrate established shop safety procedures without repeated reminders.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Instructor PPE demonstration; students inspect examples of appropriate/inappropriate PPE; individual PPE practice with immediate feedback; emergency-procedure review.
lessonVersions.assessment: Individual PPE demonstration, questioning, and instructor observation; collect WT-S1 PPE and WT-S2 Shop Safety evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Safe Equipment Use & Shop Responsibility
learningTargets: I am learning to identify safe procedures for working around welding and fabrication equipment.
I am learning to maintain a safe and organized work area.
I am learning to explain what I should do when I identify an unsafe condition.
successCriteria: I can identify potential equipment and work-area hazards.
I can follow instructor-established equipment procedures.
I can properly handle and store tools and materials.
I can maintain an organized work area and participate appropriately in cleanup.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Guided shop walkthrough focused on equipment/work areas; staged “What is wrong with this setup?” scenarios; tool/material storage and cleanup demonstration.
lessonVersions.assessment: Instructor observation, questioning, and student identification/correction of hazards; WT-S2, WT-S3, and WT-S4 evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Welding Shop Safety Verification
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate that I understand the safety requirements of the welding shop.
I am learning to identify hazards and explain appropriate corrective actions.
I am learning to demonstrate the safety knowledge necessary to begin hands-on shop activities.
successCriteria: I can demonstrate required PPE procedures.
I can identify common welding-shop hazards.
I can explain appropriate responses to unsafe conditions.
I can demonstrate sufficient safety knowledge before participating independently in shop activities.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Brief safety review through questioning; required safety assessment; practical PPE/work-area/equipment-awareness checks; targeted reteaching as needed.
lessonVersions.assessment: Safety assessment, PPE demonstration, hazard identification, instructor observation, and WT-S1 through WT-S4 evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Measurement Tools & Accurate Measurement
learningTargets: I am learning to select and use appropriate measuring tools.
I am learning to accurately measure materials used in welding and fabrication.
I am learning to understand how measurement accuracy affects fabrication quality.
successCriteria: I can select an appropriate measuring tool for the assigned task.
I can accurately read common measurements.
I can measure material and verify my measurement before marking or cutting.
I can explain how inaccurate measurements can affect a finished project.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Instructor demonstration followed by measurement stations using actual shop material; partner comparison and verification challenges.
lessonVersions.assessment: Instructor observation, questioning, measurement checks, and WT-M1 Measurement evidence.
sourceStandardsText: [ESSENTIAL] WT 2.1 - Apply mathematical concepts to measurement techniques.

lessonVersions.title: Basic Material Layout
learningTargets: I am learning to transfer measurements accurately onto material.
I am learning to use reference points and layout tools to prepare material for fabrication.
I am learning to verify my layout before cutting.
successCriteria: I can accurately transfer specified measurements to material.
I can create clear and usable layout marks.
I can use appropriate layout tools.
I can verify my layout before moving to the cutting process.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Demonstrate measurement transfer and layout on steel; compare accurate layouts with common mistakes; guided then independent practice; partner-check before instructor verification.
lessonVersions.assessment: Instructor inspection, questioning, peer verification, and WT-M2 Layout evidence.
sourceStandardsText: [ESSENTIAL] WT 2.1 - Apply mathematical concepts to measurement techniques.
WT 4.2 - Prepare layouts for cutting individual parts.

lessonVersions.title: Checking Squareness & Fabrication Accuracy
learningTargets: I am learning to check material and components for dimensional accuracy and squareness.
I am learning to recognize measurement and layout errors before they affect fabrication.
successCriteria: I can use appropriate tools to check dimensions.
I can determine whether material or components are square.
I can identify an inaccurate component or layout.
I can correct or explain how I would correct an identified error.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Accuracy challenge using prepared correct/incorrect pieces; students inspect, decide acceptability, and then check their own work.
lessonVersions.assessment: Accuracy challenge, observation, questioning, and WT-M3 Squareness & Accuracy evidence.
sourceStandardsText: [ESSENTIAL] WT 2.1 - Apply mathematical concepts to measurement techniques.

lessonVersions.title: Measurement and Layout Skill Application
learningTargets: I am learning to combine measurement, layout, and accuracy checks to prepare material for fabrication.
I am learning to work through a basic fabrication layout with increasing independence.
successCriteria: I can measure the required dimensions accurately.
I can transfer those dimensions onto material.
I can create an appropriate cutting layout.
I can check my dimensions and squareness before requesting approval to cut.
I can correct errors identified during my accuracy check.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students complete a small fabrication-layout problem using measure → layout → verify → instructor check; extension students receive tighter tolerances or complexity.
lessonVersions.assessment: Completed material layout, dimensional inspection, observation, questioning, and WT-M1/WT-M2/WT-M3 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: [ESSENTIAL] WT 2.1 - Apply mathematical concepts to measurement techniques.
WT 4.2 - Prepare layouts for cutting individual parts.

lessonVersions.title: Welding Terminology Through Shop Identification
learningTargets: I am learning to use common welding terminology correctly.
I am learning to connect welding terms to actual equipment, materials, joints, and shop operations.
successCriteria: I can identify common welding terms when shown actual shop examples.
I can use appropriate welding terminology when discussing equipment and fabrication.
I can explain selected welding terms using examples from the shop.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Brief terminology introduction followed by shop-based identification; partners explain terms using actual equipment/material; rapid identification challenge.
lessonVersions.assessment: Instructor questioning, student explanations, shop identification, and WT-K1 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 2.2 - Read, comprehend, and communicate welding terms and definitions.

lessonVersions.title: Building & Identifying Weld Joints
learningTargets: I am learning to identify common weld joint configurations.
I am learning to understand where different weld joints are used in fabrication.
successCriteria: I can identify common weld joint configurations.
I can arrange pieces of material to demonstrate different joint configurations.
I can match a joint configuration to an appropriate fabrication situation.
I can use correct terminology when describing the joint.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students use scrap steel to construct butt, lap, T-, corner, and edge joint configurations; call-and-build and identify-the-joint challenges.
lessonVersions.assessment: Hands-on joint identification/construction, questioning, observation, and WT-K2 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Identify basic weld symbols and joints.

lessonVersions.title: Connecting Welding Symbols to Real Welds
learningTargets: I am learning to identify basic welding symbols.
I am learning to connect welding symbols on a drawing to the weld or joint they represent.
successCriteria: I can identify the basic parts of a welding symbol introduced in class.
I can identify common basic weld symbols.
I can match a basic welding symbol to an appropriate physical joint or weld example.
I can explain what a basic symbol is communicating to the welder.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Short symbol demonstration; stations with physical joints/welds and symbol cards; students match and explain; arrange steel to represent displayed symbols.
lessonVersions.assessment: Symbol-to-weld matching, questioning, student explanations, and WT-K3 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Identify basic weld symbols and joints.

lessonVersions.title: Turning a Drawing Into a Fabrication Plan
learningTargets: I am learning to read dimensions and identify components on a basic fabrication drawing.
I am learning to use information from a drawing to determine what needs to be fabricated.
successCriteria: I can identify the components shown on a fabrication drawing.
I can locate and interpret required dimensions.
I can identify applicable joints or welding information.
I can explain the basic sequence I would use to begin fabricating the object.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students study a simple shop-realistic drawing and use sample material to determine needed pieces, dimensions, fit, and fabrication sequence in small groups.
lessonVersions.assessment: Drawing interpretation, material/component selection, questioning, and WT-D1 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Identify basic weld symbols and joints.
[ESSENTIAL] WT 2.1 - Apply mathematical concepts to measurement techniques. (when dimensions are actively applied)

lessonVersions.title: Drawing Lines & Communicating Fabrication Ideas
learningTargets: I am learning to recognize and use basic drawing lines.
I am learning to communicate fabrication information through a simple sketch.
successCriteria: I can identify the basic drawing lines introduced in class.
I can use appropriate lines in a simple fabrication sketch.
I can create a sketch that another person can understand.
I can include enough information for someone to recognize the intended part or assembly.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Brief line demonstration; students inspect a simple shop object and sketch it; partners interpret sketches and students revise unclear areas.
lessonVersions.assessment: Student sketch, peer interpretation, observation, questioning, WT-D2 and WT-D3 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.2 - Use appropriate lines in welding drawing.

lessonVersions.title: From Student Sketch to Shop Layout
learningTargets: I am learning to create a fabrication sketch and use it to prepare material.
I am learning to connect drawing, measurement, and layout skills to an actual shop task.
successCriteria: I can create a usable sketch with appropriate dimensions.
I can determine the material/components required from my sketch.
I can accurately transfer dimensions from my sketch onto material.
I can verify my layout before cutting or requesting instructor approval.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Small fabrication challenge using available material; sketch → measure → layout → verify; differentiate complexity/tolerance by readiness.
lessonVersions.assessment: Sketch, dimensional/layout inspection, questioning, WT-D3, WT-M1, and WT-M2 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: [ESSENTIAL] WT 2.1 - Apply mathematical concepts to measurement techniques.
WT 4.2 - Prepare layouts for cutting individual parts.

lessonVersions.title: Introduction to Thermal Cutting Equipment & Safety
learningTargets: I am learning to identify thermal cutting equipment and its major components.
I am learning to safely prepare for thermal cutting operations.
I am learning to recognize hazards associated with thermal cutting.
successCriteria: I can identify the major components of the thermal cutting equipment used in our shop.
I can identify the required PPE.
I can identify hazards associated with thermal cutting.
I can explain the basic procedures for safely operating the equipment.
I can identify unsafe equipment or work-area conditions before cutting begins.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Actual-equipment walkthrough; PPE, inspection, startup/shutdown, body-position demonstration; staged hazard hunt.
lessonVersions.assessment: Questioning, equipment identification, hazard identification, WT-T1 and WT-T2 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 4.1 - Identify and explain safety, parts, and operation of thermal cutting equipment.

lessonVersions.title: Preparing for a Thermal Cut
learningTargets: I am learning to safely prepare equipment and material for thermal cutting.
I am learning to use a layout line to guide a thermal cut.
successCriteria: I can select and wear appropriate PPE.
I can inspect and prepare the cutting area.
I can prepare material appropriately for cutting.
I can identify and follow a cutting layout.
I can explain the major steps required before beginning the cut.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Student-assisted setup; instructor demonstrates layout, positioning, setup, cut start/travel/completion and shutdown; students rehearse setup before cutting.
lessonVersions.assessment: Individual setup demonstration, PPE/work-area inspection, layout verification, WT-T2 and WT-M2 evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Guided Straight-Cut Practice
learningTargets: I am learning to safely perform a thermal cut.
I am learning to control my movement while following an established layout line.
I am learning to recognize how my technique affects cut quality.
successCriteria: I can safely prepare myself, the equipment, and the work area.
I can establish the cut correctly.
I can follow a straight layout line with improving control.
I can maintain appropriate movement during the cut.
I can safely complete the operation and secure the equipment.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Supervised straight-cut practice; first attempt focuses on safe control, then students inspect and choose one adjustment before retrying.
lessonVersions.assessment: Direct observation, completed cuts, self-evaluation, feedback, WT-T3 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: [ESSENTIAL] WT 4.3 - Perform cuts using thermal cutting processes.

lessonVersions.title: Thermal Cutting - Control & Consistency
learningTargets: I am learning to improve my control and consistency while thermal cutting.
I am learning to adjust my technique based on the quality of my previous cut.
successCriteria: I can follow an established layout with increasing accuracy.
I can maintain consistent movement during the cut.
I can inspect my completed cut.
I can identify an area of my technique that needs improvement.
I can make an appropriate adjustment on my next attempt.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Cut → inspect → adjust → cut again cycle; compare sample cuts and discuss evidence of control.
lessonVersions.assessment: Cut samples, observation, self-evaluation, questioning, WT-T3 and WT-T4 evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Evaluating Thermal Cut Quality
learningTargets: I am learning to evaluate the accuracy and quality of my thermal cuts.
I am learning to use measurement and visual inspection to determine whether a cut is usable.
successCriteria: I can measure my completed component.
I can compare the finished measurement to the required dimension.
I can visually inspect the cut edge.
I can determine whether the cut is usable for fabrication.
I can identify an adjustment that could improve my next cut.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Measure → layout → cut → measure again → inspect; students decide whether the component is fabrication-ready.
lessonVersions.assessment: Dimensional check, visual inspection, observation, questioning, WT-T4 and WT-M1 evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Cut a Component From a Fabrication Drawing
learningTargets: I am learning to use a fabrication drawing to prepare and cut a component.
I am learning to combine drawing interpretation, measurement, layout, and thermal cutting.
I am learning to work through the fabrication process with increasing independence.
successCriteria: I can identify the required component and dimensions from the drawing.
I can accurately measure and lay out the component.
I can verify my layout before cutting.
I can safely perform the required thermal cuts.
I can inspect the finished component for dimensional accuracy and cut quality.
I can determine whether my component is ready for fabrication or requires correction.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Drawing → measurement → layout → verification → cutting → inspection; checkpoints for support and tighter tolerances for extension.
lessonVersions.assessment: Completed component, drawing interpretation, dimensional/cut-quality inspection, WT-D1, WT-M1, WT-M2, WT-T3, WT-T4 evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Thermal Cutting Competency Demonstration
learningTargets: I am learning to independently demonstrate the thermal cutting skills I have developed.
I am learning to evaluate the quality and accuracy of my own work.
successCriteria: I can safely prepare myself, the work area, equipment, and material.
I can measure and create an accurate cutting layout.
I can perform a controlled thermal cut.
I can produce a usable component within established expectations.
I can inspect my work and explain what I would improve.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Individual cutting task with limited assistance; waiting students inspect samples, prepare layouts, practice another competency, or complete extension work.
lessonVersions.assessment: Individual performance demonstration; update WT-T1 through WT-T4 as applicable; targeted reteaching/reassessment for students not yet proficient.

lessonVersions.title: Introduction to SMAW Equipment & Setup
learningTargets: I am learning to identify the major components used in SMAW.
I am learning to safely prepare an SMAW welding station.
I am learning to select and use appropriate PPE for SMAW.
successCriteria: I can identify the major components of the SMAW welding station.
I can properly inspect and wear required PPE.
I can safely prepare my welding station.
I can identify unsafe equipment or work-area conditions.
I can correctly shut down and organize my station.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Brief instruction at an actual station; demonstrate power source, electrode holder, work lead, electrodes, connections, PPE, booth prep, startup/shutdown; supervised student setup.
lessonVersions.assessment: Individual setup, questioning, PPE/work-area inspection, WT-W1 and safety evidence.
sourceStandardsText: State course description - students perform SMAW (context, not a dropdown standard)

lessonVersions.title: SMAW - Striking & Restarting an Arc
learningTargets: I am learning to safely strike and establish an SMAW arc.
I am learning to restart the arc when it is interrupted.
I am learning to develop basic control of the electrode.
successCriteria: I can safely prepare my welding station.
I can strike an arc using the demonstrated technique.
I can reduce electrode sticking through improved control.
I can restart an interrupted arc.
I can safely stop welding and secure my equipment.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Short arc-striking demonstration; students move quickly to booths; try → stop → feedback → adjust → try again.
lessonVersions.assessment: Direct observation, safety procedures, questioning, WT-W2 Arc Control evidence.

lessonVersions.title: SMAW - Arc Length & Control
learningTargets: I am learning to maintain a stable SMAW arc.
I am learning to control arc length as the electrode burns.
I am learning to recognize how arc length affects my weld.
successCriteria: I can establish and maintain an arc for increasingly longer periods.
I can maintain a more consistent arc length.
I can recognize when my arc is too long or too short.
I can adjust my electrode movement while welding.
I can explain how my arc control affected the weld.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Brief demonstration; repeated booth practice focusing on arc length as the main variable; periodic weld inspection.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, weld samples, self-assessment, WT-W2 evidence.

lessonVersions.title: SMAW - Introduction to Stringer Beads
learningTargets: I am learning to produce a straight and consistent SMAW stringer bead.
I am learning to coordinate arc length, electrode angle, and travel speed.
successCriteria: I can maintain the arc throughout most or all of the bead.
I can follow the intended travel line.
I can maintain increasingly consistent bead width and appearance.
I can use appropriate electrode positioning.
I can identify one part of my technique that needs improvement.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Demonstrate stringer bead with arc length, work/travel angle, and speed; majority of period welding; students mark and explain their best bead.
lessonVersions.assessment: Weld samples, observation, self-evaluation, questioning, WT-W3 evidence.

lessonVersions.title: SMAW - Improving Bead Consistency
learningTargets: I am learning to improve the consistency of my SMAW stringer beads.
I am learning to use the appearance of my weld to make adjustments to my technique.
successCriteria: I can compare two of my welds and identify improvement.
I can recognize obvious inconsistencies in bead appearance.
I can make an appropriate adjustment to arc length, angle, or travel speed.
I can produce increasingly consistent stringer beads.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Weld → inspect → choose one adjustment → weld again; instructor prioritizes one correction at a time; extension students work to tighter consistency.
lessonVersions.assessment: Successive weld comparison, observation, student explanation, WT-W2/WT-W3 evidence.

lessonVersions.title: SMAW - Introduction to Fillet Welds
learningTargets: I am learning to apply my SMAW skills to a fillet weld.
I am learning to position the electrode appropriately for the joint.
I am learning to recognize the characteristics of an acceptable introductory fillet weld.
successCriteria: I can identify the joint and appropriate weld location.
I can position the electrode appropriately for the joint.
I can maintain reasonable arc and travel control.
I can place the weld appropriately in the joint.
I can inspect my fillet weld and identify an area for improvement.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use actual joint pieces; demonstrate setup, tack placement as appropriate, electrode position, and fillet weld; supervised practice.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, completed fillet welds, questioning, WT-W4 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Basic weld symbols and joints

lessonVersions.title: SMAW - Fillet Weld Practice & Improvement
learningTargets: I am learning to produce increasingly consistent SMAW fillet welds.
I am learning to inspect my welds and adjust my technique.
successCriteria: I can consistently position my weld within the joint.
I can maintain improving bead profile and consistency.
I can recognize obvious problems in my fillet weld.
I can use instructor feedback to make an appropriate adjustment.
I can demonstrate improvement across repeated attempts.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Primarily a welding day; repeated fillet practice with individual coaching; proficient students advance to another joint/application.
lessonVersions.assessment: Repeated weld samples, observation, visual inspection, questioning, WT-W4 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Basic weld symbols and joints

lessonVersions.title: SMAW - Applying Skills to Common Weld Joints
learningTargets: I am learning to apply SMAW skills to common joint configurations.
I am learning to adjust electrode position and technique based on the joint.
I am learning to prepare and fit components before welding.
successCriteria: I can correctly identify the assigned joint.
I can appropriately prepare and position the components.
I can select an appropriate electrode position for the joint.
I can produce a basic weld on the assigned joint.
I can inspect my work and identify needed improvements.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students prepare, fit, tack as appropriate, weld, and inspect different joint configurations; rotate applications by readiness/material availability.
lessonVersions.assessment: Joint preparation, fit-up, welds, observation, WT-W5 and WT-F2 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Basic weld symbols and joints

lessonVersions.title: SMAW - What Is My Weld Telling Me?
learningTargets: I am learning to recognize visible problems in my SMAW welds.
I am learning to connect weld appearance to possible problems with my technique.
I am learning to make adjustments based on what I observe.
successCriteria: I can identify an obvious problem in a weld.
I can use appropriate welding terminology to describe what I see.
I can identify a likely technique-related cause.
I can make a reasonable adjustment.
I can compare the next weld to determine whether my adjustment helped.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Inspect sample welds including imperfect ones; ask What do you see? What might have caused it? What would you change? Students diagnose their own work and test adjustments.
lessonVersions.assessment: Inspection discussion, diagnosis, questioning, before/after comparison, WT-W6 evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Basic weld symbols and joints

lessonVersions.title: SMAW Skill Demonstration
learningTargets: I am learning to independently demonstrate the SMAW skills I have developed.
I am learning to evaluate my completed weld and explain my welding decisions.
successCriteria: I can safely prepare and operate my SMAW station.
I can strike and maintain an arc with reasonable control.
I can produce a reasonably consistent weld.
I can complete the assigned introductory joint or fillet weld.
I can inspect my weld and identify a strength and an area for improvement.
I can make an appropriate adjustment when necessary.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Individual welding demonstration with limited assistance; waiting students practice, prepare material, inspect welds, or work on another competency; extension for proficient students.
lessonVersions.assessment: Individual performance assessment; update WT-W1 through WT-W6 as applicable; targeted practice/reassessment for Developing students.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Basic weld symbols and joints

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Planning the Build
learningTargets: I am learning to use a drawing, sketch, or project design to plan a fabrication project.
I am learning to identify the materials, dimensions, and fabrication steps required to complete a project.
successCriteria: I can explain what I am building.
I can identify the major components needed for the project.
I can determine the materials needed.
I can describe a reasonable sequence for completing the project.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Show finished example/drawing/prototype; students determine components, dimensions, joints, materials, and sequence before class discussion.
lessonVersions.assessment: Planning discussion, explanation, drawing interpretation, material identification, questioning.

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Measurement & Layout
learningTargets: I am learning to transfer dimensions from a project drawing onto material.
I am learning to prepare an accurate layout before cutting.
successCriteria: I can identify the required dimensions from the drawing.
I can accurately measure my material.
I can create clear cutting/layout marks.
I can verify my measurements before cutting.
I can correct a layout error before material is wasted.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students lay out actual components; measure twice/check once/cut once; self/partner checks before instructor approval; greater independence for consistently accurate students.
lessonVersions.assessment: Measurement/layout inspection, explanation, material preparation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Cutting Components
learningTargets: I am learning to accurately cut components for a fabrication project.
I am learning to inspect my components before moving into assembly.
successCriteria: I can safely prepare my cutting operation.
I can follow the established layout.
I can produce components that are usable for fabrication.
I can check the dimensions of my components after cutting.
I can identify a component that needs correction before assembly.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students cut actual project components and complete a quick dimensional check before moving forward; discuss appropriate cutting methods as available.
lessonVersions.assessment: Direct observation, components, dimensional/cut-quality inspection, cutting evidence.
sourceStandardsText: [ESSENTIAL] WT 4.3 - Perform thermal cuts (when thermal cutting is used)

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Fit-Up & Assembly
learningTargets: I am learning to accurately fit and position project components before welding.
I am learning to use measurements and the project drawing to verify my assembly.
successCriteria: I can position components according to the project design.
I can check alignment and squareness.
I can identify and correct unacceptable gaps or fit-up problems.
I can verify important dimensions before final welding.
I can tack components appropriately before completing the welds.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Demonstrate only needed fit-up techniques; inspect-before-weld checkpoint; partner initial fit-up check before instructor verification.
lessonVersions.assessment: Fit-up inspection, dimensional checks, observation, questioning, fabrication evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Basic weld symbols and joints (when applicable)

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Welding & Assembly
learningTargets: I am learning to apply my welding skills to an actual fabrication project.
I am learning to maintain alignment and quality while completing welded assemblies.
successCriteria: I can select an appropriate welding approach for the assigned joint.
I can safely prepare and operate my welding station.
I can place welds appropriately on the project.
I can monitor alignment and fit-up as welding progresses.
I can inspect my welds before continuing to the next fabrication step.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Majority of period project welding; individualized coaching; periodic inspection stops rather than welding the entire assembly before checking.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, weld inspection, project progress, questioning, welding evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Basic weld symbols and joints

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Inspect, Correct & Improve
learningTargets: I am learning to inspect my fabrication work against the project requirements.
I am learning to identify and correct problems before finishing my project.
successCriteria: I can compare my project to the drawing or design.
I can check important dimensions and squareness.
I can visually inspect my welds and workmanship.
I can identify an area requiring correction.
I can develop an appropriate plan for improving the problem.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Quality-control stop: drawing → project → measurements → welds → workmanship; students identify a strength and correction area; brief individual conferences.
lessonVersions.assessment: Project inspection, dimensional checks, self-evaluation, correction plan, observation.

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Finishing & Craftsmanship
learningTargets: I am learning to finish a fabricated project safely and appropriately.
I am learning to recognize how workmanship affects the quality of a finished product.
successCriteria: I can safely complete required finishing operations.
I can remove or correct appropriate fabrication defects without unnecessarily damaging the project.
I can leave the project safe to handle and use.
I can demonstrate attention to overall craftsmanship.
I can prepare my project for final inspection.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Demonstrate project-specific finishing; students compare work to General Project Rubric; use finished examples when possible.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, workmanship inspection, project-rubric evidence, final-project preparation.
sourceStandardsText: Select only WT standards actually being applied during the finishing/fabrication work that day.

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Project - Final Inspection & Evaluation
learningTargets: I am learning to evaluate a completed fabrication project using established quality expectations.
I am learning to explain how my fabrication skills developed throughout the project.
successCriteria: I can compare my finished project to its drawing/design.
I can evaluate dimensional accuracy and fit-up.
I can evaluate my welding and workmanship.
I can identify a strength in my completed project.
I can identify a skill I would improve on my next fabrication project.
I can explain the fabrication process I used.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students self-evaluate with General Welding & Fabrication Project Rubric before instructor evaluation; brief evidence-based conference.
lessonVersions.assessment: Completed project, student self-evaluation, instructor project rubric, final inspection, competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: WT 3.1 - Basic weld symbols and joints (as demonstrated)
[ESSENTIAL] WT 3.3 - Read and sketch drawings (as demonstrated)

lessonVersions.title: Welding Skills - Competency Progress Check
learningTargets: I am learning to use feedback and my competency progress to identify skills that need additional development.
I am learning to take responsibility for improving my welding and fabrication skills.
successCriteria: I can identify competencies where I have demonstrated proficiency.
I can identify competencies that still need improvement or additional evidence.
I can select an appropriate skill to practice.
I can use instructor feedback to improve my performance.
I can provide new evidence of learning when I am ready for reassessment.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Brief tracker conferences; Developing students receive targeted practice, Proficient students reassess/apply, Advanced students extend precision/complexity/leadership.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, student work, reassessment, questioning, updated tracker evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select the specific WT standards connected to competencies being reviewed or reassessed.

lessonVersions.title: Competency Reassessment & Skill Improvement
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate improvement in a welding or fabrication competency.
I am learning to apply previous feedback during a new performance attempt.
successCriteria: I can explain what I am trying to improve.
I can apply feedback from my previous attempt.
I can safely demonstrate the targeted skill.
I can provide new evidence of my current ability.
I can explain how my performance has changed.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students practice briefly before requesting reassessment; other students continue approved practice, project completion, or extension work.
lessonVersions.assessment: Individual demonstration using 0-4 rubric; update tracker using newest meaningful evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select the standards corresponding to the skills being reassessed.

lessonVersions.title: Project Completion & Final Quality Check
learningTargets: I am learning to complete and evaluate my fabrication work using established quality expectations.
I am learning to correct problems before submitting finished work.
successCriteria: I can identify the remaining work required on my project.
I can inspect dimensions, fit-up, welds, and workmanship.
I can correct appropriate problems before final evaluation.
I can safely complete finishing operations.
I can submit a project that represents my current level of craftsmanship.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students use General Project Rubric as final quality-control guide; brief conferences; finished students move to reassessment/extension.
lessonVersions.assessment: Project rubric, final inspection, observation, self-evaluation, competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: [ESSENTIAL] WT 3.3 - Read and sketch drawings (as applicable)

lessonVersions.title: Welding Shop Reset & Equipment Accountability
learningTargets: I am learning to properly care for welding equipment, tools, and the shared shop environment.
I am learning to recognize how shop organization contributes to safety and workplace efficiency.
successCriteria: I can correctly clean and organize my assigned work area.
I can properly return tools and equipment.
I can identify damaged, missing, or unsafe equipment.
I can appropriately report an equipment concern.
I can contribute to leaving the shop prepared for the next class or grading period.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Assign teams to welding stations, tools, cutting areas, tables, material storage, PPE, scrap, and consumables; teams report issues.
lessonVersions.assessment: Instructor inspection, accountability, equipment/tool check, safe cleanup observation, shop-responsibility evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Welding Skills Reflection & Next-Step Planning
learningTargets: I am learning to evaluate my progress as a welding student.
I am learning to identify strengths and areas I want to improve.
successCriteria: I can identify welding or fabrication skills that have improved.
I can identify at least one skill that still needs development.
I can use evidence from my projects, welds, cuts, or competency ratings to explain my progress.
I can establish an appropriate next skill goal.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Keep writing short; students select a physical weld/cut/project sample showing improvement, compare earlier/later evidence, and set one next skill goal.
lessonVersions.assessment: Student reflection, physical work evidence, competency discussion, questioning, next-step goal.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards connected to the competencies being reviewed; do not select every WT standard by default.

lessonVersions.title: Welding Shop Orientation & Skills Placement
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate the safety knowledge and welding-shop skills I currently possess.
I am learning to identify the appropriate starting point for my welding and fabrication instruction.
successCriteria: I can demonstrate required shop safety procedures.
I can correctly select and use required PPE.
I can explain my previous welding/shop experience.
I can demonstrate previously learned skills when appropriate.
I can accept an instructional starting point based on demonstrated evidence.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: All students begin with common safety expectations; distinguish claimed experience from demonstrated competency; returning students avoid unnecessary repetition while new/transfer students verify skills.
lessonVersions.assessment: Safety verification, PPE demonstration, experience discussion, observation, initial competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Additional standards only when students actually demonstrate those skills during placement.

lessonVersions.title: Welding Technology Skills Placement
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate the welding and fabrication skills I already possess.
I am learning to begin instruction at a level appropriate to my current abilities.
successCriteria: I can demonstrate previously learned skills safely.
I can complete assigned placement tasks with an appropriate level of independence.
I can explain the process I am using.
I can accept feedback about areas that require additional instruction.
I can demonstrate evidence supporting my competency placement.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Short practical stations may include measurement, layout, drawing interpretation, cutting, and SMAW; use only stations needed to establish evidence.
lessonVersions.assessment: Direct performance observation and initial competency ratings.
sourceStandardsText: [ESSENTIAL] WT 3.3 - Read and sketch drawings (when used)
State course description - SMAW performance (when used)

lessonVersions.title: Welding Technology - Individual Skill Pathways
learningTargets: I am learning to develop welding and fabrication skills appropriate to my current competency level.
I am learning to progress toward proficiency through practice, feedback, and demonstration.
successCriteria: I can identify my current skill focus.
I can safely complete the assigned practice or fabrication activity.
I can use instructor feedback to improve.
I can demonstrate progress toward my next competency level.
I can work increasingly independently as my skills develop.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use Instructional Pathways: Core for primary competencies; Extension for increased complexity/precision/independence; Placement for incoming students establishing appropriate starting points.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, skill demonstrations, work samples, competency evidence, and pathway movement when appropriate.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards corresponding to each group’s actual instructional focus.
