standards.wording: Identify and demonstrate general safety in accordance with government regulations, health standards, and company and/or school policy.
Demonstrate mathematical skills related to work assignments.
Communicate using welding terms and definitions from ANSI/AWS A3.0, Standard Welding Terms and Definitions.
Interpret and apply dimensions and locations of components in fabrication drawings.
Layout and fabricate according to the fabrication drawing industry standards.
Identify and explain the safety, parts, and operation of thermal cutting equipment.
Prepare layouts for cutting individual parts.
Perform cuts using thermal cutting processes.
Identify and understand the safety, parts, and operation of GMAW.
Prepare base metal for various welding processes.
Demonstrate Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW) on steel.
Visually inspect a weld.
Examine thermally cut surfaces and edges for discontinuities.
Identify and understand the safety, parts, and operation of another advanced welding process.
Prepare base metal for various welding processes.
Demonstrate another advanced welding process on steel.
Define and compare career pathways in welding technology.
Design a personal learning plan for career interest in welding technology.
Explain trends and issues in welding technology careers.
Identify and demonstrate career readiness (soft skills) in the workplace.

competencies.name: Independent Shop Safety

levels.1: Understands key safety expectations but needs frequent reminders or direct supervision.
levels.2: Usually works safely and recognizes common hazards but needs occasional prompting.
levels.3: Independently demonstrates appropriate safety during welding, cutting, and fabrication.
levels.4: Anticipates hazards, selects controls independently, explains decisions, and consistently models industry-level safe behavior.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning independent shop safety and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Equipment Safety

levels.1: Can operate assigned equipment only with step-by-step supervision.
levels.2: Completes most equipment preparation/operation/shutdown correctly with occasional checks.
levels.3: Safely prepares, operates, inspects, and shuts down assigned equipment.
levels.4: Independently verifies equipment condition, settings, and shutdown; recognizes and addresses basic equipment concerns.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning equipment safety and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Applied Measurement

levels.1: Applies basic measurements/calculations with guidance; errors may affect fit or layout.
levels.2: Applies common measurement/math skills with reasonable accuracy but needs occasional verification.
levels.3: Uses mathematical and measurement skills accurately during fabrication work.
levels.4: Selects efficient methods, verifies calculations independently, and maintains precision on more complex fabrication.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning applied measurement and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Welding Communication

levels.1: Uses some welding terminology but explanations are incomplete or imprecise.
levels.2: Uses appropriate terminology in familiar shop situations with occasional correction.
levels.3: Communicates using appropriate welding terminology.
levels.4: Communicates technical information precisely and uses terminology to explain procedures, problems, and corrective actions.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning welding communication and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Drawing Interpretation

levels.1: Locates basic dimensions/components with guidance.
levels.2: Interprets most dimensions/component locations but needs occasional clarification.
levels.3: Interprets dimensions and component locations from a fabrication drawing.
levels.4: Independently interprets complex relationships, verifies drawing information, and identifies issues before fabrication.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning drawing interpretation and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Fabrication Planning

levels.1: Can follow a provided fabrication sequence but struggles to plan one independently.
levels.2: Develops a workable sequence with teacher checkpoints or revisions.
levels.3: Determines an appropriate sequence for producing components and assemblies.
levels.4: Plans an efficient sequence independently, considering fit-up, distortion, access, quality, and rework.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning fabrication planning and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Layout

levels.1: Creates layouts with guidance; dimensional/reference errors are common.
levels.2: Creates generally accurate layouts but needs occasional checks or corrections.
levels.3: Accurately lays out components according to a fabrication drawing.
levels.4: Produces precise, efficient layouts independently and verifies dimensions/material use before cutting.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning layout and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Fabrication from Drawing

levels.1: Fabricates portions from a drawing with substantial guidance; assembly may miss key requirements.
levels.2: Produces a generally correct assembly with some dimensional or sequencing assistance.
levels.3: Produces an assembly that reasonably conforms to the provided drawing.
levels.4: Independently produces a well-fitted, dimensionally accurate assembly and documents/corrects deviations.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning fabrication from drawing and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Cutting Equipment

levels.1: Identifies basic cutting equipment/safety with prompts.
levels.2: Explains major equipment and safe operation with minor gaps.
levels.3: Identifies and explains safe operation of thermal-cutting equipment.
levels.4: Explains equipment function, hazards, setup choices, and safe operation independently and recognizes basic problems.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning cutting equipment and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Cutting Layout

levels.1: Prepares simple cutting layouts with guidance.
levels.2: Prepares generally accurate layouts but needs occasional verification.
levels.3: Prepares accurate layouts for cutting individual components.
levels.4: Plans precise, efficient layouts independently, considering reference edges, sequence, and material conservation.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning cutting layout and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Cutting Performance

levels.1: Performs cuts with close coaching; control/accuracy is inconsistent.
levels.2: Produces usable cuts with improving control and occasional assistance.
levels.3: Performs thermal cuts appropriate to the assigned fabrication task.
levels.4: Produces consistently accurate cuts on more complex tasks with strong control, efficiency, and minimal rework.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning cutting performance and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Cut Quality

levels.1: Recognizes obvious cut-surface problems after prompting.
levels.2: Identifies common discontinuities but may need help interpreting their significance/cause.
levels.3: Examines thermally cut surfaces and identifies visible discontinuities.
levels.4: Independently evaluates cut quality, connects discontinuities to likely causes, and recommends corrective action.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning cut quality and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: GMAW Equipment & Safety

levels.1: Identifies major GMAW components but needs step-by-step help for safe operation.
levels.2: Operates GMAW safely with occasional prompts/checks.
levels.3: Identifies components and safely operates GMAW equipment.
levels.4: Independently verifies equipment, gas, consumables, connections, and safe operation and explains setup decisions.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning gmaw equipment & safety and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Base-Metal Preparation

levels.1: Prepares base metal when directed but may miss cleanliness, fit, or edge-prep needs.
levels.2: Completes appropriate preparation in familiar tasks with occasional reminders.
levels.3: Properly prepares material before welding.
levels.4: Selects and performs preparation independently based on material/joint requirements and verifies readiness before welding.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning base-metal preparation and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Machine Setup

levels.1: Can enter basic settings from a chart/instructor direction but cannot yet adjust confidently.
levels.2: Selects workable settings with reference materials and makes simple adjustments with guidance.
levels.3: Selects and adjusts appropriate machine settings with decreasing assistance.
levels.4: Independently selects, fine-tunes, and explains settings based on material, joint, position, and weld response.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning machine setup and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Bead Control

levels.1: Produces beads with significant variation in profile, travel, or placement.
levels.2: Produces increasingly consistent beads with some variation or occasional coaching.
levels.3: Produces consistent GMAW beads on steel.
levels.4: Produces highly consistent beads across changing conditions and self-corrects technique/settings based on results.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning bead control and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Fillet Welds

levels.1: Produces a recognizable fillet weld but placement/profile is inconsistent.
levels.2: Produces generally acceptable fillets with some inconsistency or occasional coaching.
levels.3: Produces acceptable GMAW fillet welds.
levels.4: Produces consistently well-placed fillet welds with strong profile/consistency and independently adjusts as needed.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning fillet welds and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Joint Application

levels.1: Can weld basic joints with guidance but technique does not transfer consistently between configurations.
levels.2: Applies GMAW to common joints with partial independence and improving consistency.
levels.3: Applies GMAW to appropriate joint configurations.
levels.4: Adapts technique/settings independently across multiple joint configurations and more demanding applications.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning joint application and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Troubleshooting

levels.1: Recognizes that a weld is unsatisfactory after prompting but needs help identifying the cause.
levels.2: Identifies likely causes and makes basic adjustments with some guidance.
levels.3: Recognizes problems and adjusts settings or technique accordingly.
levels.4: Systematically diagnoses problems, tests corrections, and verifies improvement with minimal instructor input.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning troubleshooting and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Visual Weld Inspection

levels.1: Can look for obvious weld-quality features when given a checklist or prompts.
levels.2: Completes a basic visual inspection and identifies several relevant features with occasional help.
levels.3: Visually examines a completed weld.
levels.4: Performs a systematic independent visual inspection and clearly communicates findings using appropriate terminology.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning visual weld inspection and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Discontinuity Identification

levels.1: Recognizes a few obvious discontinuities with examples/prompts.
levels.2: Identifies common visible discontinuities but may confuse less familiar conditions.
levels.3: Identifies visible weld discontinuities.
levels.4: Reliably identifies and differentiates discontinuities across varied samples and explains their significance.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning discontinuity identification and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Corrective Action

levels.1: Can suggest a possible correction only with substantial guidance.
levels.2: Connects common problems to likely causes/corrections with occasional help.
levels.3: Connects observed weld problems to likely issues and identifies a reasonable correction.
levels.4: Diagnoses multiple possible causes, selects an efficient corrective action, applies it, and evaluates the result.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning corrective action and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Process Safety & Equipment

levels.1: Identifies basic process equipment/safety after instruction but needs prompting.
levels.2: Explains major equipment and safety requirements with occasional gaps.
levels.3: Identifies equipment and safety requirements for the selected advanced welding process.
levels.4: Independently explains process equipment, hazards, controls, setup considerations, and safe operating decisions.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning process safety & equipment and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Material Preparation

levels.1: Prepares material with step-by-step direction.
levels.2: Performs appropriate preparation with occasional reminders/checks.
levels.3: Prepares base metal appropriately.
levels.4: Independently selects and performs preparation based on process/joint needs and verifies readiness.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning material preparation and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Process Demonstration

levels.1: Can attempt the process with close coaching but control/consistency is limited.
levels.2: Demonstrates the process with improving control and some assistance.
levels.3: Demonstrates the selected advanced welding process on steel.
levels.4: Demonstrates consistent control independently across more challenging applications or conditions.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning process demonstration and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Advanced Application

levels.1: Applies the process only in highly guided/basic tasks.
levels.2: Applies the process with partial independence in familiar tasks.
levels.3: Applies the process with increased independence or complexity.
levels.4: Selects, applies, troubleshoots, and evaluates the process independently in complex fabrication situations.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning advanced application and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Fit-Up

levels.1: Positions components with guidance; fit/alignment often require correction.
levels.2: Achieves workable fit-up with occasional help checking alignment, gaps, or tack placement.
levels.3: Accurately prepares and positions components.
levels.4: Produces precise fit-up independently and anticipates distortion, tack sequence, access, and final dimensional effects.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning fit-up and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Fabrication Sequence

levels.1: Can follow a sequence but needs help planning or adapting it.
levels.2: Plans a workable sequence with teacher checkpoints.
levels.3: Plans and follows an efficient fabrication sequence.
levels.4: Independently optimizes sequence for efficiency, quality, distortion control, access, and minimal rework.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning fabrication sequence and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Dimensional Accuracy

levels.1: Checks dimensions when directed but may miss deviations or their impact.
levels.2: Checks key dimensions and identifies obvious deviations with occasional help.
levels.3: Checks the finished assembly against drawing requirements.
levels.4: Systematically verifies critical dimensions/tolerances, documents deviations, and determines appropriate correction.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning dimensional accuracy and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Integrated Fabrication

levels.1: Completes parts of an integrated project with substantial direction.
levels.2: Combines major fabrication skills but still needs regular checkpoints or troubleshooting help.
levels.3: Combines drawing, layout, cutting, preparation, welding, and inspection in a project.
levels.4: Independently plans, executes, inspects, troubleshoots, and evaluates an integrated fabrication project to a high standard.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning integrated fabrication and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Welding Career Knowledge

levels.1: Identifies a few welding careers with guidance but cannot yet compare requirements.
levels.2: Describes several careers and some differences in training, work, or qualifications.
levels.3: Identifies and compares welding-related career pathways.
levels.4: Independently compares pathways using training, certification, working conditions, advancement, and personal fit.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning welding career knowledge and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Personal Career Plan

levels.1: Identifies a possible career goal but plan is incomplete or highly teacher-directed.
levels.2: Creates a basic plan with reasonable next steps but needs help making it specific/realistic.
levels.3: Develops a personal learning/career plan related to welding technology.
levels.4: Creates a detailed, realistic pathway with specific training/certification/employment steps and revises it using new information.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning personal career plan and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Industry Awareness

levels.1: Can name a current welding issue/trend after instruction but explanation is limited.
levels.2: Explains a trend/issue and a basic effect on welding careers with some support.

levels.4: Connects multiple industry trends/issues to skills, technology, workforce demand, training, and personal career decisions.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning industry awareness and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

competencies.name: Workplace Readiness

levels.1: Demonstrates workplace behaviors inconsistently and needs frequent reminders.

levels.3: Demonstrates reliability, communication, teamwork, responsibility, problem-solving, and workplace behavior.

competencies.studentStatement: 1: I am learning workplace readiness and still need direct help.  2: I can do much of it but still need some help or more consistency.  3: I can do it safely and consistently with minimal help.  4: I can do it independently at a higher level and explain/troubleshoot my work.

Advanced Welding - Shop Reset & Equipment Accountability
Advanced Welding - Skills Reflection & Goal Setting
Advanced Welding - Targeted Remediation & Skill Recovery

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Welding Orientation & Safety Verification
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate advanced-shop safety practices.
I am learning to identify hazards in welding, cutting, fabrication, and material handling.
successCriteria: I can identify and correct hazards.
I can prepare work areas and equipment safely.
I can work safely with minimal prompting.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Brief orientation followed by hands-on PPE, equipment, work-area, and hazard verification. Use realistic shop scenarios; provide targeted support for new/transfer students.
lessonVersions.assessment: Individual safety demonstration, observation, questioning, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Prior-Skill Verification
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate the welding and fabrication skills I bring into Advanced Welding.
I am learning to identify skills I am ready to advance and skills needing development.
successCriteria: I can demonstrate prior skills safely.
I can measure and prepare material accurately.
I can show appropriate equipment setup.
I can produce evidence of current ability.
I can identify an area for practice.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use short practical stations: measurement, layout, equipment setup, welding sample, cutting, and inspection.
lessonVersions.assessment: Direct performance observation, sample inspection, questioning, and initial/updated competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 1.1 (Essential); select additional standards only for skills actually demonstrated

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Workplace Expectations
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate workplace behaviors expected in an advanced welding environment.
I am learning to take responsibility for equipment, productivity, quality, and cleanup.
successCriteria: I can clean without repeated reminders.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Evaluate the process during a short shop task and connect behaviors to employer expectations.
lessonVersions.assessment: Workplace/shop-practice observation, questioning, and career-readiness evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Measurement & Precision Verification
learningTargets: I am learning to apply measurement and mathematical skills with greater accuracy during fabrication.
I am learning to verify measurements before cutting or assembly.
successCriteria: I can work with increasing independence.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use real material and tighter tolerances; students compare measurements and resolve discrepancies with tools.
lessonVersions.assessment: Measurement demonstration, layout/material, calculation checks, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Applied Fabrication Math
learningTargets: I am learning to use mathematical reasoning to solve fabrication problems.
I am learning to apply calculations to actual material.
successCriteria: I can select a mathematical process.
I can transfer dimensions to material.
I can verify results before cutting.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use real shop problems: component length, spacing, material totals, equal divisions, and project calculations.
lessonVersions.assessment: Calculation, material application, dimensional verification, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Welding Terminology
learningTargets: I am learning to use technical welding terminology correctly in the shop.
I am learning to communicate fabrication information using industry language.
successCriteria: I can identify terminology for current processes.
I can use correct terms for equipment, joints, welds, and operations.
I can explain a shop operation accurately.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Teach vocabulary beside actual equipment, weld samples, joints, drawings, and shop operations.
lessonVersions.assessment: Questioning, shop discussion, student explanation, and technical-knowledge evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Interpreting Fabrication Drawings
learningTargets: I am learning to interpret a fabrication drawing before beginning work.
I am learning to use drawing information to develop a fabrication plan.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students analyze a realistic drawing and compare proposed fabrication plans before instructor discussion.
lessonVersions.assessment: Drawing interpretation, fabrication plan, questioning, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Drawing-to-Material Layout
learningTargets: I am learning to transfer fabrication drawing information accurately onto material.
I am learning to verify layout before fabrication.
successCriteria: I can correct layout problems independently.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students complete layouts with self-check and peer verification before instructor approval.
lessonVersions.assessment: Completed layout, dimensional inspection, observation, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Fabrication Sequence & Problem-Solving
learningTargets: I am learning to plan an efficient fabrication sequence.
I am learning to anticipate problems before cutting, fitting, or welding.
successCriteria: I can determine a logical sequence.
I can explain order of operations.
I can begin with minimal direction.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Give scenarios where sequence matters; challenge plans with access, distortion, and squareness questions.
lessonVersions.assessment: Fabrication sequence, explanation, problem-solving discussion, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Drawing-to-Fabrication Challenge
learningTargets: I am learning to independently use a drawing to produce an accurate component.
I am learning to combine drawing interpretation, math, measurement, layout, and fabrication.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Provide drawing and material without a step-by-step procedure: interpret, plan, measure, layout, fabricate, inspect.
lessonVersions.assessment: Finished component, dimensional inspection, drawing conformance, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Thermal Cutting Safety & Setup Verification
learningTargets: I am learning to independently prepare thermal cutting equipment and work area.
I am learning to verify condition and setup before cutting.
successCriteria: I can complete setup/shutdown with minimal help.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Brief review followed by individual setup verification and intentionally incorrect setup scenarios.
lessonVersions.assessment: Setup demonstration, hazard identification, questioning, and observation.

lessonVersions.title: Precision Thermal Cutting
learningTargets: I am learning to perform thermal cuts with increased accuracy and consistency.
I am learning to control technique to produce fabrication-ready components.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use dimensional cutting challenges and the cycle measure, layout, cut, measure, inspect, adjust.
lessonVersions.assessment: Cuts, dimensional checks, technique observation, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Drawing-Based Cutting
learningTargets: I am learning to use a fabrication drawing to prepare and cut a component independently.
I am learning to combine drawing, measurement, layout, and cutting.
successCriteria: I can judge readiness for fabrication.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students receive a component drawing and material, determine sequence, cut, and self-inspect.
lessonVersions.assessment: Drawing interpretation, component, dimensions, cut quality, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Cut Inspection
learningTargets: I am learning to visually inspect a thermal cut using quality expectations.
I am learning to distinguish acceptable cuts from those needing correction.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Sort real cut samples into Accept, Correct/Rework, Reject and justify with observable evidence.
lessonVersions.assessment: Inspection activity, explanation, questioning, and competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 6.2; AWT 4.3 when cutting is also demonstrated

lessonVersions.title: Cutting Troubleshooting
learningTargets: I am learning to connect cut-quality problems to setup/equipment/technique causes.
I am learning to adjust the process based on inspection.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use Cut, Inspect, Diagnose, Adjust, Cut Again, Compare; lead with questions instead of answers.
lessonVersions.assessment: Before/after cuts, diagnosis, adjustments, observation, and competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Thermal Cutting Competency Demonstration
learningTargets: I am learning to independently demonstrate advanced thermal cutting and inspection.
I am learning to evaluate accuracy and quality.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Individual drawing-based cutting task with limited instructor assistance.
lessonVersions.assessment: Performance demonstration, component, dimensional/cut inspection, explanation, tracker update.

lessonVersions.title: GMAW Equipment & Safe Setup
learningTargets: I am learning to identify major GMAW components.
I am learning to safely prepare GMAW equipment.
I am learning to recognize how setup affects performance.
successCriteria: I can prepare work lead/gun/wire/gas as applicable.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Demonstrate at the machine, then pairs identify components and complete supervised setup; include incorrect-setup scenarios.
lessonVersions.assessment: Equipment/setup demonstration, questioning, safety observation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: GMAW Machine Settings & Variables
learningTargets: I am learning to identify important GMAW settings and variables.
I am learning to recognize how changes affect performance.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Demonstrate controlled setting changes: Setting, Weld, Result; students predict outcomes.
lessonVersions.assessment: Predictions, setting identification, weld comparison, technical evidence.

lessonVersions.title: GMAW Base-Metal Preparation
learningTargets: I am learning to prepare steel appropriately for GMAW.
I am learning to recognize how material condition and fit-up affect quality.
successCriteria: I can prepare weld area safely.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students inspect steel in different conditions and prepare their own material.
lessonVersions.assessment: Material inspection/preparation, questioning, observation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: First GMAW Beads
learningTargets: I am learning to establish and maintain a controlled GMAW weld.
I am learning to coordinate gun movement while observing the puddle.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Short demonstration followed quickly by booth time using Weld, Look, Feedback, Adjust, Weld Again.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, weld samples, self-evaluation, GMAW evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Travel Speed & Gun Control
learningTargets: I am learning to control travel speed and gun position.
I am learning to recognize how movement affects bead appearance.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Repeated beads focusing on one variable; students select and explain their most consistent bead.
lessonVersions.assessment: Weld samples, observation, comparison, explanation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: GMAW Bead Consistency
learningTargets: I am learning to produce increasingly consistent GMAW welds.
I am learning to visually inspect and use results to improve.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use Weld, Inspect, Diagnose, Adjust, Weld Again with successive comparison.
lessonVersions.assessment: Weld samples, inspection, diagnosis, observation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: GMAW Fillet Weld Fundamentals
learningTargets: I am learning to apply GMAW to a fillet-weld joint.
I am learning to control placement/profile.
I am learning to inspect the weld.
successCriteria: I can prepare and fit joint.
I can inspect and identify improvements.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Demonstrate fit-up, tack-up, gun position, and technique, then maximize practice time.
lessonVersions.assessment: Fit-up, fillet welds, inspection, observation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: GMAW Fillet Weld Development
learningTargets: I am learning to improve fillet weld consistency and quality.
I am learning to use visual evidence to choose adjustments.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Hands-on welding with one highest-priority correction at a time.
lessonVersions.assessment: Repeated welds, before/after inspection, observation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: GMAW Joint Applications
learningTargets: I am learning to apply GMAW skills to different joint configurations.
I am learning to adjust technique for joint geometry and position.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Rotate through appropriate joints; students prepare, fit, tack, weld, and inspect.
lessonVersions.assessment: Joint prep, fit-up, welding, inspection, questioning, competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 5.3 (Essential); AWT 6.1 (Essential); AWT 3.1 when drawings are used

lessonVersions.title: GMAW Settings Troubleshooting
learningTargets: I am learning to distinguish settings/equipment problems from technique problems.
I am learning to troubleshoot using weld evidence.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use controlled or naturally occurring problems; ask what they see, cause, first change, and evidence.
lessonVersions.assessment: Diagnosis, adjustment, before/after comparison, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Formal Visual Weld Inspection
learningTargets: I am learning to systematically visually inspect a weld.
I am learning to communicate quality observations using appropriate terminology.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Inspection table with real samples: Accept, Improve/Rework, Reject, with evidence-based justification.
lessonVersions.assessment: Inspection activity, explanations, classification, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Drawing-Based GMAW Fabrication
learningTargets: I am learning to use GMAW in a complete drawing-based fabrication process.
I am learning to independently plan, fabricate, weld, and inspect an assembly.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Small drawing-based challenge: Drawing, Plan, Material, Layout, Prep, Fit-Up, Tack, Weld, Inspect.
lessonVersions.assessment: Assembly, dimensions, GMAW performance, inspection, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: GMAW Competency Demonstration
learningTargets: I am learning to independently demonstrate expected GMAW skills.
I am learning to evaluate performance and justify quality assessment.
successCriteria: I can weld with limited help.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Individual performance task; others continue targeted practice or extension work.
lessonVersions.assessment: Performance demonstration, inspection, preparation, explanation, tracker update.

lessonVersions.title: Introduction to [Selected Advanced Process]
learningTargets: I am learning to identify equipment/components/basic principles of the selected process.
I am learning to safely prepare to use the process.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Introduce at the actual station, compare with known processes, then practice identification/setup/shutdown.
lessonVersions.assessment: Equipment identification, setup, safety observation, questioning.

lessonVersions.title: [Selected Advanced Process] Setup & Variables
learningTargets: I am learning to correctly set up the selected process.
I am learning to recognize variables that influence performance.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Demonstrate setup and controlled variable changes; students predict outcomes.
lessonVersions.assessment: Setup, questioning, variable identification, result comparison.

lessonVersions.title: [Selected Advanced Process] Material Preparation
learningTargets: I am learning to prepare material appropriately for the selected process.
I am learning to recognize how preparation affects quality.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students inspect material in varying conditions and prepare their own pieces.
lessonVersions.assessment: Material inspection/preparation, questioning, observation.

lessonVersions.title: [Selected Advanced Process] First Welds
learningTargets: I am learning to establish and control the selected process.
I am learning to coordinate movements required for a basic weld.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Short demonstration, then hands-on practice using Attempt, Inspect, Feedback, Adjust, Attempt Again.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, weld samples, self-evaluation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: [Selected Advanced Process] Control & Consistency
learningTargets: I am learning to produce increasingly consistent welds.
I am learning to use visual inspection to improve technique.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Maximize welding time using Weld, Inspect, Diagnose, Adjust, Weld Again.
lessonVersions.assessment: Samples, inspection, observation, explanation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: [Selected Advanced Process] Joint Application
learningTargets: I am learning to apply the selected process to a welded joint.
I am learning to adjust technique for joint configuration.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Move from basic practice into real joints; students prepare and fit their own pieces where practical.
lessonVersions.assessment: Fit-up, welding, completed joint, inspection, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: [Selected Advanced Process] Troubleshooting & Correction
learningTargets: I am learning to diagnose problems with the selected process.
I am learning to distinguish equipment, settings, material, and technique causes.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use actual student problems and question through diagnosis before correction.
lessonVersions.assessment: Diagnosis, adjustment, before/after comparison, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: [Selected Advanced Process] Performance Demonstration
learningTargets: I am learning to independently demonstrate the selected process.
I am learning to evaluate work and explain needed adjustments.
successCriteria: I can complete weld/joint with limited help.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Individual performance task while others practice, inspect, fabricate, or extend.
lessonVersions.assessment: Performance demonstration, weld, inspection, explanation, tracker update.

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Project Analysis & Planning
learningTargets: I am learning to analyze a fabrication drawing and develop a build plan.
I am learning to identify materials, dimensions, joints, requirements, and challenges.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Present drawing/design without giving the fabrication sequence; students propose and compare plans.
lessonVersions.assessment: Drawing interpretation, fabrication plan, questioning, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Material Planning & Estimation
learningTargets: I am learning to determine material needed for a project.
I am learning to plan material use efficiently before cutting.
successCriteria: I can create efficient cutting plan.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use actual available stock dimensions; students plan how to obtain all components efficiently.
lessonVersions.assessment: Material list, calculations, cutting plan, instructor review.

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Layout
learningTargets: I am learning to transfer fabrication information accurately from drawing to material.
I am learning to verify critical dimensions before cutting.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students use self-check, peer check when appropriate, then instructor check only when needed.
lessonVersions.assessment: Layout inspection, dimensional verification, observation, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Producing Project Components
learningTargets: I am learning to produce components meeting drawing requirements.
I am learning to inspect components before assembly.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students fabricate real project components and inspect before assembly: do not weld a bad part into a good project.
lessonVersions.assessment: Components, dimensions, cut inspection, observation, competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 3.2 (Essential); AWT 4.3 when used; AWT 6.2 when inspecting cuts

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Fit-Up, Alignment & Tack-Up
learningTargets: I am learning to accurately fit and align components before final welding.
I am learning to use tack-up and verification to maintain dimensions.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use the hold point Fit, Measure, Square, Tack, Measure Again, Weld.
lessonVersions.assessment: Fit-up inspection, dimensions, tack quality, questioning, observation.

lessonVersions.title: Choosing the Welding Process
learningTargets: I am learning to select an appropriate welding process for a fabrication task.
I am learning to justify decisions based on material, joint, equipment, and requirements.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Where possible, students choose and defend a process; if specified, explain why it fits the application.
lessonVersions.assessment: Process selection, justification, equipment preparation, observation.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 5.3 (Essential) and/or AWT 7.3 (Essential), plus applicable fabrication standards

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Project Welding
learningTargets: I am learning to apply advanced welding skills to an assembly.
I am learning to maintain dimensions and quality during welding.
successCriteria: I can identify problems before continuing.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Primarily shop work; instructor coaches and asks students to use drawing/fabrication plan to decide next steps.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, welding, inspection, progress, dimensions, competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Distortion, Alignment & Correction
learningTargets: I am learning to monitor dimensional changes during fabrication.
I am learning to identify and correct alignment/fabrication problems.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Turn actual project problems into What happened, Why, Correct, Prevent troubleshooting cycles.
lessonVersions.assessment: Dimensional checks, diagnosis, corrective action, explanation.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 3.2 (Essential); AWT 6.1 (Essential); AWT 2.1 when dimensions are checked

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Quality-Control Inspection
learningTargets: I am learning to inspect a fabricated assembly using quality expectations.
I am learning to determine whether work meets drawing/workmanship requirements.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students perform QC with drawing and project rubric before instructor grading; peer QC may be used.
lessonVersions.assessment: Student inspection, rubric evidence, dimensions, weld/cut inspection, instructor verification.

lessonVersions.title: Project Correction & Rework
learningTargets: I am learning to use inspection results to improve fabricated work.
I am learning to safely correct workmanship or fabrication problems.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Require Identify, Plan, Correct, Reinspect before rework begins.
lessonVersions.assessment: Correction plan, rework, final inspection, questioning, competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards directly connected to the correction; likely AWT 3.2, AWT 6.1, AWT 6.2, and applicable process standards

lessonVersions.title: Finishing & Professional Workmanship
learningTargets: I am learning to complete a project to an appropriate professional level.
I am learning to recognize the difference between finished and well finished.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Compare technically complete work with stronger craftsmanship; students prepare projects for final inspection.
lessonVersions.assessment: Workmanship inspection, progress, observation, project-rubric evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select only standards actually demonstrated during finishing

lessonVersions.title: Final Advanced Project Evaluation
learningTargets: I am learning to evaluate completed fabrication using established expectations.
I am learning to explain and defend fabrication decisions.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students self-assess with the General Welding & Fabrication Project Rubric before instructor evaluation/conference.
lessonVersions.assessment: Completed project, self-assessment, instructor rubric, competency evidence, final inspection.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards actually demonstrated; likely AWT 3.2, 5.3, 6.1, 6.2, 7.3 as applicable

lessonVersions.title: From Work Order to Finished Product
learningTargets: I am learning to interpret a fabrication assignment as a workplace task.
I am learning to identify information needed before work.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use a simulated work order connected to an actual shop task; students plan before beginning.
lessonVersions.assessment: Work-order interpretation, fabrication plan, questioning, career-readiness evidence.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 9.1 (Essential); AWT 3.1 when drawing used; AWT 3.2 when fabrication begins

lessonVersions.title: Workplace Quality & Accountability
learningTargets: I am learning to take responsibility for the quality of work I produce.
I am learning to inspect work before passing it on.
successCriteria: I can explain why quality matters.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Evaluate fabricated examples and ask whether students would send them to a customer or next production step.
lessonVersions.assessment: Inspection, explanation, quality decisions, career/inspection evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Workplace Productivity - Efficient, Safe & Accurate
learningTargets: I am learning to organize work to be productive without sacrificing safety or quality.
I am learning to distinguish efficiency from rushing.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Small production-style task; students plan materials, tools, equipment, sequence, inspection and discuss lost time.
lessonVersions.assessment: Work-habit observation, completed task, quality check, discussion.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 9.1 (Essential); add technical standards actually performed

lessonVersions.title: Workplace Teamwork & Fabrication
learningTargets: I am learning to work effectively with others during fabrication.
I am learning to communicate responsibilities, measurements, problems, and progress.
successCriteria: I can verify information before handoff.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Team task with rotating roles such as layout, preparation, fit-up, welding, and inspection.
lessonVersions.assessment: Team performance, individual responsibility, communication, finished product.

lessonVersions.title: Workplace Communication & Problem-Solving
learningTargets: I am learning to professionally communicate fabrication problems.
I am learning to explain a problem clearly before asking someone else to solve it.
successCriteria: I can describe checks already made.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use realistic scenarios such as wire-feed issues, short parts, drawing/material mismatch, or out-of-square assemblies.
lessonVersions.assessment: Student explanation, troubleshooting communication, questioning.

lessonVersions.title: Receiving & Using Feedback
learningTargets: I am learning to receive workplace feedback and use it to improve performance.
I am learning to respond productively to correction.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Give one specific process/quality correction during real shop work and require immediate application.
lessonVersions.assessment: Application of feedback, corrected work, observation.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 9.1 (Essential); add the technical standard for work being improved

lessonVersions.title: Welding & Fabrication Careers
learningTargets: I am learning to identify career pathways connected to welding and fabrication.
I am learning to connect course skills to workplace opportunities.
successCriteria: I can identify an area of interest.
I can explain possible next training.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Conversational career exploration tied to student interests; invite local industry/technical-school voices when practical.
lessonVersions.assessment: Discussion, questioning, brief career-interest evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Preparing for a Welding Opportunity
learningTargets: I am learning to present my welding experience and skills professionally.
I am learning to prepare for employment, training, or apprenticeship opportunities.
successCriteria: I can identify application information needed.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use short shop-floor interview conversations instead of a paperwork-heavy resume day.
lessonVersions.assessment: Professional responses, accurate skill description, career-readiness evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Welding Workplace Performance Challenge
learningTargets: I am learning to combine technical welding skills with workplace expectations.
I am learning to complete a fabrication assignment safely, accurately, productively, and professionally.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Run a mini simulated workday using a fabrication work order; evaluate safety, organization, productivity, communication, problem-solving, quality, tool care, and cleanup.
lessonVersions.assessment: Completed task, observation, project/competency evidence, quality inspection, workplace criteria.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 9.1 (Essential); AWT 3.2 (Essential); plus technical standards required by the task

lessonVersions.title: Competency Progress Check
learningTargets: I am learning to evaluate my current welding and fabrication competencies.
I am learning to use evidence and feedback to determine what I need to improve next.
successCriteria: I can select a skill goal.
I can use time toward goal.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students review tracker evidence and choose Placement, Core, or Extension work; brief conferences as needed.
lessonVersions.assessment: Goal selection, observation, practice, questioning, competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards connected to competencies being reviewed/practiced

lessonVersions.title: Targeted Competency Reassessment
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate improvement in a welding or fabrication competency.
I am learning to apply previous feedback during a new performance attempt.
successCriteria: I can perform with increased independence.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students practice before requesting individual reassessment; classmates continue approved work.
lessonVersions.assessment: Individual 0-4 competency demonstration and tracker update using newest meaningful evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select exact standards corresponding to skills being reassessed

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Open Shop - Competency Development & Fabrication
learningTargets: I am learning to independently identify and develop a skill appropriate to my competency level.
I am learning to use Open Shop to improve, reassess, complete, or extend skills.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Placement: targeted instruction; Core: competency/project/reassessment; Extension: advanced application, precision, independence, troubleshooting.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, weld/cut/project inspection, reassessment, project progress, tracker evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select specific AWT standards actively applied that Friday

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Fabrication - Project Completion
learningTargets: I am learning to complete fabrication work to drawing, quality, and workmanship expectations.
I am learning to identify and correct deficiencies before submission.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students use drawing and project rubric for final QC before instructor evaluation; finished students reassess or extend.
lessonVersions.assessment: Project inspection, rubric evidence, observation, competency evidence, completed project.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards demonstrated by project; likely AWT 3.2, 5.3, 6.1, 6.2, 7.3 as applicable

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Welding - Shop Reset & Equipment Accountability
learningTargets: I am learning to maintain equipment, tools, materials, and work areas to workplace expectations.
I am learning to take responsibility for our shared shop.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Assign shop zones and conduct a workplace-style reset for the next shift/class.
lessonVersions.assessment: Instructor inspection, accountability, tool/equipment check, safety/career evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Welding - Skills Reflection & Goal Setting
learningTargets: I am learning to evaluate my development as an advanced welding student.
I am learning to use evidence from my work to establish my next technical goal.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Minimal writing; students use actual work evidence to explain Where I Started, What Improved, Evidence, What Comes Next.
lessonVersions.assessment: Student explanation/reflection, work evidence, competency discussion, next-step goal.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards connected to competencies actually reviewed

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Welding - Safety & Entry Verification
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate safety knowledge and technical skills I bring into Advanced Welding.
I am learning to establish an instructional starting point from evidence.
successCriteria: I can work safely in placement.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: All verify safety; returning students move to Core/Extension while new/transfer students complete placement.
lessonVersions.assessment: Safety verification, experience discussion, observation, initial competency evidence.

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Welding - Skills Placement Challenge
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate my current welding and fabrication abilities.
I am learning to begin Advanced Welding at a level appropriate to demonstrated skills.
successCriteria: I can complete placement tasks independently.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Use only needed practical stations: measurement/layout, drawing, setup, cutting, GMAW, visual inspection.
lessonVersions.assessment: Direct performance observation, work samples, explanation, inspection ability, initial ratings.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards corresponding to placement tasks; possible AWT 2.1, 3.1, 3.2, 4.x, 5.x, 6.1

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Welding - Individual Instructional Pathways
learningTargets: I am learning to develop welding and fabrication skills appropriate to my current competency level.
I am learning to progress toward greater proficiency, quality, and independence.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Placement: targeted foundations/verification; Core: primary competencies; Extension: complexity, precision, troubleshooting, design, advanced processes.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, demonstrations, project samples, inspection evidence, tracker updates.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards corresponding to each group’s actual work

lessonVersions.title: GMAW - Targeted Skill Development
learningTargets: I am learning to improve my GMAW performance through focused practice, inspection, and adjustment.
I am learning to take greater responsibility for diagnosing and improving my own welding.
successCriteria: I can identify the GMAW skill I need to improve.
I can safely practice the targeted skill.
I can inspect my results and make an evidence-based adjustment.
I can demonstrate progress through subsequent attempts.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Placement: foundational GMAW instruction; Core: targeted practice; Extension: additional joints, tighter quality expectations, troubleshooting, or fabrication applications.

I can make an evidence-based adjustment.

lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, weld samples, inspection, explanation, reassessment, tracker evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select applicable AWT 7.x and AWT 6.1 standards

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Fabrication - Project Work Day
learningTargets: I am learning to independently apply welding and fabrication skills to my current project.
I am learning to manage my fabrication sequence, quality, and productivity.
successCriteria: I can identify my current step and what comes next.
I can select and safely use appropriate equipment.
I can work from the drawing or plan.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Individualized project work, instructor coaching, targeted demonstrations, peer collaboration where appropriate, and quality-control checks.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, project progress, drawing conformance, weld/cut inspection, rubric and competency evidence.
sourceStandardsText: Select exact standards connected to the current fabrication stage

lessonVersions.title: Advanced Fabrication - Completion, Remediation & Extension
learningTargets: I am learning to use my progress and feedback to determine my next fabrication goal.
successCriteria: I can identify what I need to complete, correct, or improve.
I can select an appropriate task.
I can work safely and independently.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Placement: foundations; Core: current project/competency completion; Extension: complexity, tighter tolerances, design, or advanced-process application.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, project progress, reassessment, rubric evidence, extension work.
sourceStandardsText: Select standards based on each student’s current activity

lessonVersions.title: Welding Shop - Workplace Performance
learningTargets: I am learning to demonstrate professional work habits while completing welding and fabrication tasks.
successCriteria: I can care for tools and equipment.
I can solve appropriate problems independently.
lessonVersions.engagementStrategies: Students complete normal welding/fabrication work while workplace behaviors are deliberately observed.
lessonVersions.assessment: Observation, competency evidence, project progress, workplace-performance criteria.
sourceStandardsText: AWT 9.1 (Essential), plus standards associated with technical work

learningTargets: I am learning to strengthen a welding or fabrication skill that has not yet reached proficiency.
I am learning to use targeted feedback and additional practice to improve my performance.
successCriteria: I can identify the skill requiring improvement.
I can explain what needs to change.
I can safely practice the targeted skill.
I can demonstrate improvement through new evidence.
